ReaderProfile.title: ReaderProfile
ReaderProfile.description: Represents a profile for a user who reads content and can subscribe to news notifications. This entity stores information about individual readers, separate from content creators.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ReaderProfile entity.

email.description: The email address of the reader, primarily used for sending notifications and as a unique identifier for login. This email must be unique across all reader profiles.

name.description: The display name or full name of the reader.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the reader profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the reader profile was last updated.

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Manages a reader's subscription status for receiving news notifications via email, typically a general platform-wide news feed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subscription entity.

readerId.description: Reference to the ReaderProfile who owns this subscription. (Relationship: ReaderProfile 1:N Subscription)

subscribedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the subscription was initially created or activated.

isActive.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the subscription is currently active. If false, the reader should not receive notifications.

definition.description: Stores individual reader profiles. The document ID (`{readerId}`) corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID of the reader, enabling path-based ownership. The 'id' field within the document should match the document ID for self-validation.

params.name: readerId
params.description: The unique identifier (Firebase Auth UID) of the reader. This serves as the document ID for the reader's profile.

definition.description: Stores individual subscription records for a specific reader. The 'readerId' field within each document is denormalized from the parent path for authorization independence, allowing security rules to verify ownership without `get()` calls. The 'id' field within the document should match the document ID for the subscription.

params.name: readerId
params.description: The unique identifier (Firebase Auth UID) of the parent reader, owning this subscription.

params.name: subscriptionId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific subscription document.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be minimalistic, secure, and highly efficient, focusing exclusively on managing reader profiles and their subscriptions, as content management is delegated to Sanity.io. 

**Authorization Independence:** This design achieves authorization independence by using a hierarchical path structure combined with explicit denormalization. For `ReaderProfile` documents, the document ID (`{readerId}`) directly corresponds to the Firebase `request.auth.uid` of the authenticated user. This means a user's profile is found at `/readerProfiles/{request.auth.uid}`, making access checks immediate and atomic without requiring `get()` calls to other documents.

For `Subscription` documents, they are nested under the `ReaderProfile` at `/readerProfiles/{readerId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`. Critically, each `Subscription` document *also* contains a `readerId` field within its data (`resource.data.readerId`). This denormalization ensures that security rules can verify ownership (i.e., `request.auth.uid == readerId` from the path AND `request.auth.uid == resource.data.readerId` from the document data) without needing to fetch the parent `ReaderProfile` document. This allows for atomic creation, update, and deletion of subscriptions.

**Querying for Authorization and Security Rules (QAPs):** The structure inherently supports secure `list` operations (QAPs) by leveraging path-based ownership. A reader can easily query their own profile at `/readerProfiles/{request.auth.uid}`. Similarly, a reader can query all their subscriptions by listing documents under `/readerProfiles/{request.auth.uid}/subscriptions`. The security rules would enforce that the `readerId` wildcard in the path matches `request.auth.uid`, effectively filtering results to only the current user's data. This prevents unauthorized users from performing wide `list` queries across all profiles or subscriptions, fulfilling the QAP principle by moving authorization filtering to the path and explicit document fields rather than relying on `get()` calls or complex rule logic.

**Structural Segregation and Access Modeling:** Each collection (`/readerProfiles` and `/readerProfiles/{readerId}/subscriptions`) has a homogeneous security posture. All documents within `/readerProfiles` are private to the `readerId` specified in the path. Similarly, all `Subscription` documents are private to their parent `readerId`. This clear segregation simplifies security rules significantly, making them easy to write, understand, and debug.
